images.title: Elaine Cox / Lough Derg from Arra Mountains
images.caption: Lough Derg from Arra Mountains. The walk is rich in flora and fauna, with hedgerows and forested sections hosting a variety of wildflowers, including bluebells in spring. Birds such as robins, blackbirds, and chaffinches can often be heard and seen, while kestrels may be spotted hovering above the hill's slopes. Lough Derg below supports a wealth of wildlife, including herons, swans, and other waterfowl, contributing to the natural beauty of the area. The mix of natural and historical elements makes this walk a memorable experience.

images.title: Graves of the Leinstermen (3) - Information board by P L Chadwick, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Graves of the Leinstermen 1. According to local legend, the warriors were defeated by the forces of Brian Boru, the High King of Ireland, in a conflict over control of the area. The site holds cultural and historical significance, as it reflects Ireland’s medieval power struggles and the enduring legacy of Brian Boru. The graves themselves are a collection of stone-lined structures, which are thought to be the remains of a cairn or burial mound. Though the exact origins and nature of the graves are unclear, the site has become an important landmark in Irish folklore and heritage. From the ridge, visitors can enjoy spectacular views over the surrounding countryside and Lough Derg, adding to the site's appeal.

images.title: Graves of the Leinstermen by David P Howard, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Graves of the Leinstermen. The area is surrounded by natural beauty, with rugged landscapes, rolling hills, and diverse wildlife. The route to the site passes through scenic trails where walkers may encounter wildflowers, ferns, and native trees, as well as birds such as skylarks and buzzards. The combination of historical intrigue and stunning vistas makes the Graves of the Leinstermen a fascinating destination.

description: This walk climbs to the Millennium Cross on Laghtea Hill in the Arra Mountains of County Tipperary. The hill is located just east of Lough Derg and provides fine views over the lake and surrounding hills. The walk starts near the historic Graves of the Leinstermen. This ancient burial site is traditionally believed to mark the resting place of Leinster warriors who fell in battle during the 10th or 11th century. and then heads north to the hill. The trail then follows a mix of quiet country lanes and forested paths, eventually leading to the hill summit where the cross is situated. The Millennium Cross was erected in 2000 to commemorate the turn of the millennium and serves as a striking landmark overlooking Lough Derg. The area around Laghtea Hill has a long history, with evidence of ancient settlements in the surrounding region, reflecting its importance as a vantage point and strategic location. As you ascend, the changing landscape offers a mix of open pasture, wooded areas, and panoramic vistas of the lake and its islands. At the summit, the cross itself is a focal point for visitors, providing an ideal spot to rest and take in the views. On a clear day, you can see for miles across the lush countryside, making the climb particularly rewarding. You can continue your walking in the area on the Graves Of The Leinster Men and Tountinna Walk .
